[[26]] can’t you learn to say that one word? Say ‘Catano’ or I’ll kill you!” But the parrot would not say it. Many times the man screamed, “Say ‘Catano’ or I’ll kill you!” But the bird would not [[27]] the name.
Finally the man gave up. He picked up the parrot and threw the bird into the chicken house. In the chicken house, there were four old chickens, waiting to be killed [[28]] Sunday’s dinner. “You are even more stupid than the chickens,” the man said as he was leaving.

sections.title: 三、閱讀測驗（20%）
sections.instructions: 說明：第41至50題，每題請分別根據各篇文章選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題第一部分」。每題答對得2分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage:
One of the most unusual graduation speakers of the 1983 commencement season was not a person at all. The speaker was Robot Redford, a robot who delivered the commencement address at a community college in suburban Maryland.
The speaker, carefully programmed, arrived on the stage under its own power and proceeded to tell the audience of 658 graduates, their families, and friends that they would have to learn to work with robots and technology to solve society’s problems. The robot described itself as an extension of a person to help humans increase the workload. Although this particular robot can be programmed to speak, the voice heard wasn’t that of the robot, because it was feared that the robot’s voice was not loud enough to carry throughout the hall. An amplified voice of a human was used instead, while the listeners watched the robot.
Robot Redford was followed by a person, William Bakaleinikoff, who spoke about the need for cooperation between people and technology. Mr. Bakaleinikoff’s experience with his topic included the fact that he had created Robot Redford and had provided the voice for the robot’s words to the graduates.
There was quite a bit of controversy over the choice of a robot as a commencement speaker. Some students thought it was insensitive and degrading to use a robot. Others thought the idea was clever and innovative.
“I’ll never forget this speech,” said one graduate. “You forget a political leader, but you won’t forget a robot.”

questions.stem: Robot Redford’s speech was discussed in this article mainly because ______.
Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.A: Robot Redford was a talking machine.

options.C: Robot Redford made a graduation speech in 1983.
options.D: Robot Redford graduated from a college in Maryland.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements can be supported by the passage?

options.A: A robot was designed to let humans decrease their productivity.
options.B: Robot Redford was the brainchild of William Bakaleinikoff.
options.C: Everybody in the commencement was pleased with the arrangement.
options.D: Robot Redford’s speech was too difficult to understand.

tags.topic: a robot as a college commencement speaker

groups.passage: Summers with father were always enjoyable. Swimming, hiking, boating, fishing--the days were not long enough to contain all of our activities. There never seemed to be enough time to go to church, which disturbed some friends and relatives. Accused of neglecting this part of our education, my father still instituted a summer school for my brother and me. His summer course included ancient history, which Papa felt our schools neglected, and <u>navigation</u>, in which we first had a formal examination in the dining room, part of which consisted of tying several knots in a given time limit. Then we were each separately sent on what was grandly referred to as a cruise in my father’s 18-foot boat, spending the night on board, and loaded down, according to my mother, with enough food for a week. I remember that on my cruise I was required to formally plot our course, using the tide table, even though our goal was an island I could see quite clearly across the water in the distance.

groups.passage:
PARIS, Dec. 9 -- Paris will be given a new Eiffel Tower--but made of wood--for the millennium, city mayor Jean Tiberi said Tuesday, presenting a program of celebration for the year 2,000 which would transform the “city of light” into the “capital of light.”
The new structure will be 200 meters high, 100 meters shorter than the cast-iron Eiffel Tower built 100 years ago.
It will be made of timber as an ecological symbol of “the right to a dignified life on a protected Earth,” said architects Normier, Henni and Lelievre, who were also responsible for the Europe section at the Seville exhibition.
The tower, of pinewood, will be built on eight pillars and will be topped with a flower of five metal petals of 700 square meters each.
The structure, to be erected in the redeveloped areas of the capital’s 13th district, will cost 250 million francs (US$42 million).
Tiberi also said that Paris would be placed under the sign of the lights of “culture and life” and “intelligence.”
“If, in 1900, Paris was consecrated the ‘city of light’, it will become the ‘capital of light’ for the millennium,” Tiberi said.
The mayor said new buildings would be illuminated, notably along the banks of <u>the Seine</u>, which would become a luminous strip, while Notre Dame Cathedral would be lit from the inside to show off its stained glass windows.
A laser clock would be installed on top of the Arc de Triomphe at the top of the Champs Elysees and three laser beams would pick out the hands showing the hours, minutes and seconds in the millennium countdown, Tiberi said.
A giant egg-timer will be set up in the Place de la Concorde and its sand will begin running after a solar eclipse scheduled on April 11, 1999.

options.A: The old Eiffel Tower must be torn down.
options.B: The old iron Eiffel Tower needs to be re-built with wood.
options.C: The tower is built to celebrate the Seville exhibition.
options.D: The tower is built to celebrate the coming of the year 2,000.

What is “the Seine” mentioned in the passage?

refers_to.note: 原卷底線（選文 notably along the banks of the Seine）

options.B: The name of the new tower.

options.A: To serve as a symbol of environmental concerns.
options.B: To reduce the weight and ensure the safety.
options.C: Out of the consideration of the limited budget.
options.D: To form a contrast with the iron structure of the old tower.

groups.passage:
April Rain Song
by Langston Hughes

Let the rain kiss you.
Let the rain beat upon your head with silver liquid drops.
Let the rain sing you a lullaby.

The rain makes still pools on the sidewalk.

The rain plays a little sleep-song on our roof at night－

sections.title: 二、英文作文（20%）
sections.instructions:
說明：1.請依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長以120字左右為原則。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem:
提示：
每個人在不同的情況下對雨可能有不同的感受。請寫一篇短文，敘述你在某一個下雨天的實際經歷或看到的景象，並據此敘述你對雨的感覺。

tags.topic: a real rainy-day experience or scene and one’s feelings about rain

extraction.method: 官方 Word 版（paper-2.doc → soffice 轉 docx → python-docx，依 run 的底線屬性辨識空格與畫底線字）取文字，與 pdftotext -layout 題本逐段比對；以 Read 逐頁檢視題本 PDF 影像（8 頁，含封面）確認版面、段落、粗體／斜體／底線；答案檔為國文、英文、數學合併的掃描檔（無文字層），以 pdftoppm 200dpi 轉圖並裁切英文欄，用 Read 看影像逐題抄錄。查證者：60題選擇題答案以 Read 看答案檔 300dpi 英文欄影像逐題重新比對；題幹、選項、選文以 docx 文字與 pdftotext 全文逐字（含標點）比對，並以 Read 檢視題本全部頁面影像確認段落、底線與空格位置。
issues: 題號跳號（查證者修正）：題本封面印「單一選擇題共60題（1~50題及61~70題）」，選擇題第一部分為第1–50題、第二部分為第61–70題，題本本來就沒有第51–60題（答案檔英文欄同樣是 1–50、61–70）。為符合 schema「題號從 1 連續」的規則（validator 不允許跳號，不能留 error），第二部分10題的 no 改為內部連續序號 51–60，label 保留題本／答案檔的原題號 "61"–"70"；選文空格依 schema 規定對齊 no，寫成 [[51]]–[[60]]（[[51]] 即題本的 (61)，依此類推至 [[60]] 即 (70)）。答案依原題號對照官方答案檔：61 I、62 K、63 F、64 L、65 H、66 B、67 C、68 J、69 A、70 E，與 no 51–60 一一對應。instructions 仍逐字保留「第61至70題」。前端顯示題號與選文空格時應使用 label（no→label 對照），不要直接顯示 no。
第61–70題：題本此大題沒有「文意選填」等名稱，標題只有「貳：選擇題（第二部分）　（10%）」（中間為全形空格，照 Word 版保留）；格式為一篇短文10個空格搭配 (A)–(L) 12個共用選項（其中 (D) Therefore、(G) interested 未被使用），依格式歸為 word_bank，小題 mode 為 bank_choice。

短詩閱讀（非選擇題一）：依 schema type 表「舊卷的信函、短詩閱讀」歸為 other，小題 mode 為 short_answer，並加 item_type 標註。題本印題號 1.–5.，與選擇題第1–5題重號，因此 no 保留 1–5、label 改為「短詩1」–「短詩5」；英文作文題本未編號，no 填 1、label 為「作文」（同 gsat-89／gsat-90 慣例）。validator 的「題號重複 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]」warning 因此產生，屬合理。
非選擇題答案：答案檔（answer.pdf，國文、英文、數學合併的掃描檔）只有選擇題答案；大考中心未公布短詩閱讀第1–5題的參考答案或評分原則，也沒有作文評分說明，answer／accepted_answers／scoring_notes 均填 null。
無統計資料：units.json 中87學年度只有題本 PDF、Word 版與選擇題答案，沒有 stats（答對率／鑑別度／選項分析）與 scoring 檔，所有小題 stats 為 null，sources.scoring／stats 為空陣列（validator 的「整份考卷沒有任何統計資料」warning 屬實）。

結構核對：gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 83–87 期別只有粗略描述（「87單一選擇題60題（1~50題及61~70題）」、非選擇題兩大題），與本卷一致。本卷實際結構：壹 選擇題（第一部分）—一、字彙、片語與語法 1–20（每題1分，20分）、二、綜合測驗 21–40（每題1分，20分）、三、閱讀測驗 41–50（每題2分，20分）；貳 選擇題（第二部分）61–70（每題1分，10分）；參 非選擇題—一、短詩閱讀 5題×2分（10分）、二、英文作文（20分）；合計100分，考試時間100分鐘（封面）。
第16–20題為兩人對話形式的單題（各題獨立，不是題組），放在詞彙大題 s1g1，stem 以換行分隔每位說話者的台詞。

空格位置：第22、32、39題的空格在題本緊接前面的標點（word--(22)、alone.”(32)、infection.(39)，之間無空格；Word 版底線 run 也證實），依原樣寫成 word--[[22]]、alone.”[[32]]、infection.[[39]]。第21–30題選文第2段、第4段在 Word 版因排版被硬換行拆成多個段落，對照 PDF 頁面影像（縮排位置）合併回原本的段落。

畫底線的字：第44題問 “navigation”、第49題問 “the Seine”，兩者在題本選文中畫底線，passage 以 <u>navigation</u>、<u>the Seine</u> 標記（v1.1 判讀：Word 檔 run 底線屬性與 PDF 第5、6頁影像確認是底線，維持 <u>，並填 refers_to）；題幹中同字串在題本以引號表示、無底線，照原樣。第42、45題的 NOT 在題本為粗體，短詩第5題的 boring、harsh 等六個形容詞為斜體，依規則不保留格式。
逐字保留：短詩第6行行末為全形破折號「－」（U+FF0D），照題本保留；第47–50題選文的 the year 2,000（含千分位逗號，第47題選項 (D) 亦同）、Champs Elysees（無重音符號）、PARIS, Dec. 9 -- Paris 照題本保留。Word 版句號後的雙空格已壓成單一空格。
短詩 passage：首兩行為詩名 April Rain Song 與作者 by Langston Hughes（題本分別置中、靠右），之後空一行接詩文，三節之間以空行分隔。各題組前的「21-30題為題組」等說明列未存入。
標註：grammar_point 中的 enough_to（第18題）、indirect_question（第20題）、noun_clause（題本第65、70題，即 label 65、70）為 schema 範例以外的值；第16、18、37、38題答案為非詞類單位（不定詞／副詞片語／比較結構／分詞），未填 answer_pos。
